old: At its root is an ancient word for simply losing your footing and dropping.
It once named the moment a musical phrase falls silent at its close.
It's a hidden twin of both 'cadenza' and 'chance,' all born from the same Latin word for falling.
clues: This noun for a pattern in sound or motion comes from a Latin verb meaning to fall. It first described a musical phrase falling to its close.
It is the rise and fall of a speaking voice, or the steady beat of marching feet: more of a lilting, patterned flow than plain rhythm.
Cyclists track their pedaling one. It shares its old falling root with the word chance and with cadenza, a soloist's showy flourish.
